MINUTES
  SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  FEBRUARY 27, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A special meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City
Hall.

2.  PRESENTATION
CHAIR SCHACHTER introduced herself as the new Chair of the Equestrian Committee.

3.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Ciarolla, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano,
  Robinson, Harik, and Schmitz
  Committee Members Absent:  Griggs, Medawar, and Martin
  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 23, 2023
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JANUARY 23, 2023,
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.
5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  NONE.
6.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  UPDATE REGARDING PORTUGUESE BEND HORSE SHOW’S REQUEST FOR
  ARENA #2 RENOVATION
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a verbal overview per written
  report.
  Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed that turn outs would still be possible in
  response to MEMBER SILVANO.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
FEBRUARY 27, 2023
  1
   Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the new footing would not be affected by turn
  outs in response to MEMBER SHINN.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the renovation could be completed in time for this
  year’s show. Superintendent Goldsmith responded affirmatively adding that the
  contractor would be able to blend the footing on site.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas shared that MEMBER GRIGGS, who
  was unable to attend the meeting, expressed that she was in favor of the new
  footing for Arena #2.
  MEMBER HARIK asked for confirmation of the 50% cost share with PBNHS.
  Carole Rowe, 2023 PBNHS Chair, stated that she thought the revised quote would
  be at much lower cost. She stated that the vendor had agreed to donate footing to
  Peninsula Committee Children’s Hospital (PCCH) for the PBNHS and was
  concerned that the revised quoted was high.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he would connect with the contractor to
  confirm the cost.
  MEMBER SILVANO stated that having an organization like the PBNHS who is
  willing to partner with the City at any level is helpful in offsetting the full cost.
  MEMBER NILSEN asked if there are other vendors for the project. Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that West Coast Footings is local. CHAIR SCHACHTER
  added that the vendor also volunteers services for the PBNHS.
  Louise Koch, Audience Member, asked about the difference between the Western
  Blend and the Pleasure Blend noted in the report. Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that the mixture of both are the same and that both names are used to describe
  the new product. He added that the footing is a GGT blend that is shallow like that
  in the Chandler arena and has less fabric in it. Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that all the sand would have to be removed but would be used in other arenas, in
  response to Ms. Koch.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that West Coast Footings would come in
  prior to the show to redistribute the footing in Arena 1 in response to Ms. Koch’s
  question regarding the depth of Arena 1 footing. Ms. Rowe stated PBNHS was
  hoping some of the footing in Arena 1 could be removed for the show and then put
  back afterward. Superintendent Goldsmith stated it could be discussed further
  during show planning. He explained that Arena 1 requires a lot of water and that
  when not enough water is used, it can be deep. CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that
  Arena 1 is similar to Chandler Arena and that the rain helps.
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER NILSEN to:
  APPROVE THE PROPOSAL FOR RENOVATION OF ARENA 2 WITH A
  SHARE OF COSTS WITH THE PORTUGUESE BEND NATIONAL HORSE
  SHOW AND RECOMMEND IT TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
FEBRUARY 27, 2023
  2
   COMMISSION FOR REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATION TO CITY
  COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL.

  AYES: Brtis, Harik, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano, Robinson, Ciarolla, and Schachter
  ABSENT: Griggs, Martin and Medawar

  The motion carried.

B.  ESTABLISHMENT OF SUBCOMMITTEE FOR PORTUGUESE BEND HORSE
  SHOW’S REQUEST FOR RENOVATIONS TO ARENAS 3 AND 4
  CHAIR SCHACHTER provided a verbal overview per written report and asked who
  from the Committee had interest in joining the subcommittee.
  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that MEMBER GRIGGS, who was unable to attend
  the meeting, expressed that she was interested in joining the subcommittee.
  After discussion, it was determined that MEMBER GRIGGS, MEMBER NILSEN,
  MEMBER SILVANO and MEMBER SHINN would be on the subcommittee. It was
  also decided that Supervisor Pinuelas would connect with the Palos Verdes
  Chapter of the California Dressage Society and the Palos Verdes Peninsula
  Horsemen’s Association to inquire about representatives from their organizations.
  Ms. Rowe shared that she would let staff know who would represent PBNHS on
  the subcommittee.
  Assistant City Manager Davis recommended the Subcommittee’s timeline be open
  ended and that updates could be provided at Committee meetings in response to
  CHAIR SCHACHTER.
C.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUE LOG
  MEMBER SHINN reported the trail by Moccasin has been muddy and slippery as
  a result of rain. MEMBER SILVANO confirmed that the gates to the landfill have
  been getting locked earlier in response to MEMBER HARIK.
D.  HORSE TRAINER LIST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reviewed the trainer list provided in the agenda packet and
  explained that some additional trainers were still being processed and have not
  yet been added to the list. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she will reach out to
  Laurie Barnett regarding trail rides in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

E.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a review of the revised equestrian recognition
  projects as previously approved and stated that donations can still be made for the
  Carol Dean Porter project.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
FEBRUARY 27, 2023
  3
   CHAIR SCHACTER provided a reminder of Carol Dean Porter’s many
  contributions over the years to the community.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she would send information to the PVPHA
  regarding this final push for donations.

F.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROJECTS LIST

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief verbal overview per written report, adding that
  staff would be looking to add two additional items to the list: Trimming of trees near
  the newly installed fitness equipment at Ernie Howlett Park and drainage
  improvements by the Tennis Center.

  ACM Davis stated the Arena 2 Renovation project would be added to the list if
  approved by Council in response to MEMBER SILVANO.

  Superintendent Goldsmith confirmed that all the Dapplegray arenas will be
  replenished in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated the chain link fence up between Harbor Sight Dr.
  to George F Canyon would not be permanent in response to MEMBER
  ROBINSON. He added that he would look into it further to confirm the timeline.

  MEMBER CIAROLLA asked about using asphalt chips to replace the missing
  asphalt pieces on the trails. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he has yet to
  find a suitable material to use but that he would stockpile the material once he
  does.

  MEMBER HARIK stated the trail at George F Canyon was not in a good state.

  MEMBER BRTIS inquired about the impact of Rolling Hills Little League’s
  sprinklers on the trail noting that the trail can be very wet. Superintendent
  Goldsmith noted that asphalt chips would be good for that area and that it could
  also be resloped.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
FEBRUARY 27, 2023
  4
 8.  ADJOURNMENT

  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER NILSEN to:
  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:46 p.m. TO THE NEXT EQUESTRIAN
  MEETING SCHEDULED TO BE HELD ON MONDAY, MARCH 27, 2023,
  AT 7:00 P.M.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Pam Brown Schachter, Chair
  Community Services Supervisor
